question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $20{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 25 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+4\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot (-2)}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3+4}{1+0+4} \\  & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
20{x}_{2}=20\cdot \frac{7}{5}=28.
$$
